identity.title: AffectGPT: A New Dataset, Model, and Benchmark for Emotion Understanding with Multimodal Large Language Models
identity.version: PMLR v267, ICML 2025 proceedings; 22-page PDF including Appendices A–N

summary: A constant all-basic-label prediction maximizes the primary basic-emotion HIT score without observing inputs; four of nine headline components use this metric. This disclosed limitation materially limits the benchmark's recognition interpretation. Later source selects test-maximal checkpoints, but provenance tying that behavior to published tables is unresolved.
limitations: No author-code execution, model inference, training or raw empirical reproduction
Later released source commit dated2026-10-13 not proven to generate2025 tables
Large data, weights and binary prediction outputs excluded from supplied snapshot

problems.title: Basic-emotion hit rate has an input-independent optimum
problems.source_claim: Section4 describes basic emotion recognition as selecting the most likely basic label and defines Eq13 HIT as mapped reference membership in variable-size predicted set; four Table2 primary columns and 4/9 of mean use HIT.
source_locations: PDF pp6–7 §4 Eq13 and disclosure paragraph
PDF p7 Table2 and p21 Table12
assumptions: Every ground-truth y_i belongs to Y
Variable-cardinality predicted sets with no exclusivity/cardinality constraint
Same pointwise grouping G_k applied to both reference and prediction
For omitted-unmapped implementation, at least one reference remains; result evaluated on retained subset
Metric-input sets considered directly; no claim a specific caption always parses to that set
problems.suspect_step: Reference coverage is used as primary evidence of selecting the most likely basic emotion although additional labels never decrease the score.

complete_check.analytic: Choose predicted set Y for every sample; y_i in Y implies G_k(y_i) in G_k(Y), so every retained indicator=1 for every wheel. Adding labels monotonically increases or preserves HIT. This predictor uses no input.

numeric_scope.stress_interpretation: Holds five other scores fixed and replaces four basic scores by all-label optimum; not a trained model, actual ranking reversal, score improvement or estimated bias

counterevidence: Authors explicitly disclose no false-positive metric afterEq13; extra labels may be valid fine-grained emotions
HIT remains a legitimate reference-coverage diagnostic
No evidence AffectGPT actually emits all labels or relative model ordering reverses
Sentiment WAF and fine-grained setF are outside this particular all-label optimum
problems.core_dependency: MER-UniBench is a named core contribution; four primary datasets and4/9 of headline mean cannot distinguish selective recognition from a constant universal label list.
problems.severity_rationale: Demonstrated material core evaluation harm; disclosed status does not remove the logical limitation. Major does not require invalidating dataset/model contributions, actual score loss or difficult repair.

repair.statement: For the most-likely-basic-label claim require one prediction from fixed basic vocabulary and score canonicalized accuracy; preserve free-description coverage as a separately named diagnostic with appropriate fuller labels/human evaluation for extra-label correctness.
repair.verification: Analytic: singleton HIT reduces to accuracy on chosen label space and universal multi-label output is inadmissible.
repair.limits: No actual re-scoring; no guarantee all free-form evaluation problems are fixed; single-label ground truth does not automatically justify precision against extra fine-grained labels.

focused_check.method: Relevant frozen source passages/static source, existing actual check output and independent analytic integration; no author-code execution.
focused_check.conclusion: For every retained reference label, a constant set containing every raw label contains its pointwise mapped label and obtains HIT=1. The disclosed lack of false-positive penalty and auxiliary specificity statistic do not restore discrimination in the reported HIT aggregation. Major is retained for this core metric limitation; the 88.8211 stress mean holds other columns fixed and is not a measured model result.

problems.title: The later release selects checkpoints using test scores
problems.source_claim: Paper Table2 and related comparisons are described as model performance; supplied later README recommends scripts whose aggregate selects per-dataset test-maximal checkpoint.
source_locations: Supplied AffectGPT README ScoreCalculation and inference epochs30–60
assumptions: Multiple eligible prediction files are present for a test-selection effect
get_test_name2gt corresponds to actual test labels, verified for MER2023 andIEMOCAP loaders
Historical paper impact additionally requires the published tables to have used this routine/candidate set, which is not established

complete_check.static: Loads testlabels then computes each checkpoint's primary score and selects np.argmax; aggregator calls separately for each of nine datasets with unrestrictedtest_epochs=''.

finite_example.interpretation: Two different estimands; not a published-bias estimate

counterevidence: A single independently selected result file yields no additional selection among checkpoints
Original table-generating code or protocol may differ
No saved binary outputs or historical logs examined
problems.core_dependency: If used historically with multiple candidates, would alter interpretation of headline and ablation scores as held-out performance of fixed selected models.
problems.severity_rationale: Paper-level validity/provenance unresolved; pending evidence does not increase supported severity. Later code behavior is directly established.
required_evidence: Candidate prediction-file manifest and chosen epoch IDs per dataset

repair.statement: Fix checkpoint selection with independent validation before test evaluation; specify common versus task-specific checkpoint and report held-out scores.
repair.verification: Protocol-level conditional recommendation only; no historical repair verified

evidence: Static source hashes and line anchors in initial_checks.json

focused_check.method: Relevant frozen source passages/static source, existing actual check output and independent analytic integration; no author-code execution.
focused_check.conclusion: The released scorer selects eligible-file maxima separately using test-label scores; multiple candidate files are necessary for the oracle discrepancy. One independently selected file is a limiting exception. The later commit is not bound to the published runs, so historical benchmark attribution correctly remains Needs Evidence.

scoped_non_findings: Eq7 fusion dimensions consistent; no softmax requirement inferred
Table2 means andTable3/5 differences arithmetically consistent
Fine-grained metric uses harmonic mean of averagedP/R as defined; empty/zero boundary convention needs clarification, no observed experimentalfailure
Table7 has20 independent sampled videos with4 raters, not80 independentvideoobservations
AppendixF states individual-model selection criterion, so higher combined-pair score is not an established error
No train/test contamination, fabrication or licensing violation inferred

focused_scope_check.result: The metric's disclosed limitation is treated as a reproduced core consequence, not an undisclosed discovery. The later repository, missing raw predictions/data and partial figure coverage remain bounded. Historical scores and empirical effects are not independently reproduced.
